title: In-Context Learning
hook: Paste a few examples into a prompt and a large language model performs the task - no gradient updates, no fine-tuning, the prompt is the program.
key_points: The model adapts to a new task by reading examples in its context window, not by changing its weights.
GPT-3 popularized three regimes: zero-shot (task description only), one-shot (one example), and few-shot (a handful).
Performance scales with model size - small models barely benefit from examples, large ones improve substantially.
ICL is not fully understood: models may be pattern-matching on format rather than learning the underlying rule.
content_html: When Brown and colleagues at OpenAI released GPT-3 in 2020, they highlighted a surprising capability: the model could perform tasks it had never been explicitly trained on, given just a few labeled examples in the prompt. They called this "in-context learning" (ICL), and it reframed how practitioners think about deploying large language models.
extra_html:
How it works

The model's weights are frozen at inference time. Instead, you format a handful of (input, output) pairs as plain text and prepend them to your query. The model, having learned statistical patterns across a huge corpus during pre-training, infers the task from the examples and generates an appropriate continuation. No gradient steps occur - the "learning" is entirely in the forward pass over the context window.

Why it matters

ICL turned prompting from a curiosity into a practical tool: you can adapt a single model to translation, classification, parsing, or almost any structured task by writing good examples rather than collecting labeled datasets for fine-tuning. It also raised deep questions about what large models are actually doing at inference time - questions still being actively studied. GPT-3 (Brown et al., 2020) introduced the term; for a fuller tour of the methods and open puzzles, see Dong et al.'s survey on arXiv.

related.title: GPT-3: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
related.hook: Show the model a few examples right in the prompt and it picks up the task — no fine-tuning, no gradient updates. GPT-3 turned prompting into the new programming.

related.title: Large Language Models Are Zero-Shot Reasoners
related.hook: Appending 'Let's think step by step' to a prompt unlocks multi-step reasoning with zero examples - chain-of-thought without the example-writing overhead.

related.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
related.hook: Ask a big model to 'think step by step' and its math and logic scores jump. Reasoning was there all along — you just had to ask it to show its work.
